# `silk/tls/certificate_text`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Text forms of certificate fields as OpenSSL prints them: object names, distinguished names,
validity times, and serial numbers.

## When to use
Use it to show a certificate the way OpenSSL and Node.js do, such as `X509Certificate.subject`,
`issuer`, `validFrom`, `serialNumber`, and `signatureAlgorithm` in Node.js, or the `DirName`
entries of `subjectAltName`.

## Details
[`CertificateText.objectName`](#CertificateText.impl.objectName) looks up the short and long names of an object identifier in
the object table of OpenSSL 3.0, and [`CertificateText.writeObjectIdentifier`](#CertificateText.impl.writeObjectIdentifier) writes the
dotted form, such as `1.2.840.113549.1.1.11`.

[`CertificateText.writeName`](#CertificateText.impl.writeName) writes a DER `Name`, such as `Certificate.subjectDer`, in one
of the [`NameTextFormat`](#NameTextFormat) layouts. It decodes BMPString, UniversalString, and the 8-bit string
types to UTF-8 and escapes as RFC 2253 does. It checks the strings as OpenSSL does when it
reads a name, so a name that OpenSSL rejects is an error here too.

[`CertificateText.writeTime`](#CertificateText.impl.writeTime) writes a [`CertificateTime`](./tls-certificate.md#CertificateTime) as `Jan  2 03:04:05 2025 GMT`, and
[`CertificateText.writeSerial`](#CertificateText.impl.writeSerial) writes a serial number in upper-case hexadecimal.

## Errors
- [`CertificateTextError`](#CertificateTextError) for DER that is not valid, or an output that is too short.

## Gotchas
The text is for display and logs. Compare names by their DER, not by this text: two
different names can print the same. The object table is the one of OpenSSL 3.0, so a
newer identifier prints in dotted form.

## Examples
### Print a subject
```silk
import silk.core.result { Result }
import silk.collections.slice { Slice }
import silk.tls.certificate_text { CertificateText, CertificateTextError, NameTextFormat }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  // SEQUENCE { SET { SEQUENCE { commonName, UTF8String "a,b" } } }
  let name = b"\x30\x0e\x31\x0c\x30\x0a\x06\x03\x55\x04\x03\x0c\x03\x61\x2c\x62"
  let mut text: [u8; 16] = [0; 16]
  let length = match CertificateText.writeName(name, NameTextFormat.Multiline, &mut text) {
    Result<usize, CertificateTextError>.Success { value } => value
    Result<usize, CertificateTextError>.Failure { error: _ } => {
      return 1
    }
  }
  // The comma is escaped: CN=a\,b
  if length != 7 || text[4] != 92 {
    return 2
  }
  return 42
}
```

Import as `CertificateText` with `import silk.tls.certificate_text { CertificateText }`.

<a id="NameTextFormat"></a>

## `NameTextFormat`

```silk
pub enum NameTextFormat
```

How [`CertificateText.writeName`](#CertificateText.impl.writeName) lays out a distinguished name.

<a id="NameTextFormat.Multiline"></a>

### `Multiline`

```silk
Multiline
```

One attribute per line in the order of the DER, such as `C=US\nO=Example\nCN=example.com`,
with ` + ` between the attributes of one RDN. Control characters are escaped as `\XX`.
Node.js uses it for `X509Certificate.subject` and `issuer` (OpenSSL's
`XN_FLAG_SEP_MULTILINE` with `ASN1_STRFLGS_ESC_2253`, `ESC_CTRL`, and `UTF8_CONVERT`).

<a id="NameTextFormat.Rfc2253"></a>

### `Rfc2253`

```silk
Rfc2253
```

RFC 2253: the RDNs in reverse order, separated by `,`, with `+` inside an RDN, such as
`CN=example.com,O=Example,C=US`. An attribute with an unknown type, or a value that is not
a string, is written as `#` and the hexadecimal DER of the value. Control characters are
not escaped. Node.js uses it for the `DirName` entries of `subjectAltName` (OpenSSL's
`XN_FLAG_RFC2253` without `ESC_CTRL` and `ESC_MSB`).

<a id="CertificateText.impl.objectName"></a>

### Associated function `objectName`

```silk
pub fn objectName(identifier: &[u8]) -> Option<ObjectName>
```

Returns the names of the object identifier whose DER content is `identifier`, or `None`
when the object table of OpenSSL has no entry for it.

<a id="CertificateText.impl.namedObject"></a>

### Associated function `namedObject`

```silk
pub fn namedObject(name: &[u8]) -> Option<ObjectName>
```

Returns the object whose short name or long name is `name`, as OpenSSL's `OBJ_txt2nid`
finds it: short names first, then long names. The match is exact and case-sensitive.

<a id="CertificateText.impl.objectIdentifierLength"></a>

### Associated function `objectIdentifierLength`

```silk
pub fn objectIdentifierLength(identifier: &[u8]) -> Result<usize, CertificateTextError>
```

Returns the length in bytes of [`CertificateText.writeObjectIdentifier`](#CertificateText.impl.writeObjectIdentifier).

#### Errors
- `InvalidEncoding` as with [`CertificateText.writeObjectIdentifier`](#CertificateText.impl.writeObjectIdentifier).

<a id="CertificateText.impl.writeObjectIdentifier"></a>

### Associated function `writeObjectIdentifier`

```silk
pub fn writeObjectIdentifier(identifier: &[u8], output: &mut [u8]) -> Result<
    usize,
    CertificateTextError,
  >
```

Writes the dotted form of the object identifier whose DER content is `identifier`, such as
`2.5.4.3`, to the start of `output` and returns its length, as OpenSSL's `OBJ_obj2txt`
does with numeric output.

#### Errors
- `InvalidEncoding` if `identifier` is empty, a sub-identifier has a leading `0x80` byte or
  is not finished, or an arc has more than 1024 decimal digits.
- `OutputTooSmall` if `output` is shorter than the text.

<a id="CertificateText.impl.writeName"></a>

### Associated function `writeName`

```silk
pub fn writeName(name: &[u8], format: NameTextFormat, output: &mut [u8]) -> Result<
    usize,
    CertificateTextError,
  >
```

Writes the DER `Name` `name` as text in `format` to the start of `output` and returns its
length. An empty name is empty text.

#### Details
Each attribute is its short name from the object table, or its dotted identifier, then `=`
and the value. A UTF8String is written as it is, the 8-bit string types as Latin-1, and
BMPString and UniversalString as UTF-8. `"`, `+`, `,`, `;`, `<`, `>`, and `\` are escaped
with `\`, and so are a leading space or `#` and a trailing space.

#### Errors
- `InvalidEncoding` if the DER is not valid or not minimal, or a value is a type or string
  that OpenSSL rejects in a name: a UTF8String that is not UTF-8, a BMPString or
  UniversalString with a surrogate or a bad length, or a tag such as INTEGER.
- `OutputTooSmall` if `output` is shorter than the text.

<a id="CertificateText.impl.writeTime"></a>

### Associated function `writeTime`

```silk
pub fn writeTime(time: CertificateTime, output: &mut [u8; 24]) -> usize
```

Writes `time` as OpenSSL's `ASN1_TIME_print` does, such as `Jan  2 03:04:05 2025 GMT`, to
the start of `output` and returns its length. The day is padded to two places with a
space and the year is not padded.

<a id="CertificateText.impl.serialLength"></a>

### Associated function `serialLength`

```silk
pub fn serialLength(serial: &[u8]) -> Result<usize, CertificateTextError>
```

Returns the length in bytes of [`CertificateText.writeSerial`](#CertificateText.impl.writeSerial).

#### Errors
- `InvalidEncoding` if `serial` is empty.

<a id="CertificateText.impl.writeSerial"></a>

### Associated function `writeSerial`

```silk
pub fn writeSerial(serial: &[u8], output: &mut [u8]) -> Result<usize, CertificateTextError>
```

Writes the big-endian signed integer `serial`, such as `Certificate.serial`, in
upper-case hexadecimal to the start of `output` and returns its length, as OpenSSL's
`BN_bn2hex` does: whole bytes without leading zero bytes, such as `0A1B`, `0` for zero,
and `-` before the magnitude of a negative number.

#### Errors
- `InvalidEncoding` if `serial` is empty.
- `OutputTooSmall` if `output` is shorter than the text.
